theme: The year of the LORD’s favor; the divine warrior
readingInstruction: Read Isaiah 61:1-63:14. In chapter 61 an anointed one announces good news, which Jesus read aloud in the synagogue at Nazareth. Then comes a vision of a divine warrior and a long memory of the exodus. Read 61:1-3 as if you were in that synagogue.
settingTheScene: Isaiah 61 is a text that Jesus chose to read at the beginning of his public ministry (Luke 4:16-21). It describes an anointed herald who announces release to captives. Chapter 62 speaks of Zion’s new name and of God’s delight in her as a bridegroom delights in his bride. Chapter 63 opens with a figure coming from Edom in blood-stained garments, treading the winepress of wrath, and ends with a remembrance of God’s saving acts in the exodus.
observation: “The Spirit of the Lord GOD is upon me, because the LORD has anointed me to bring good news to the poor” (61:1).
“To proclaim liberty to the captives, and the opening of the prison to those who are bound” (61:1).
“To proclaim the year of the LORD’s favor, and the day of vengeance of our God” (61:2).
“To grant to those who mourn in Zion… a beautiful headdress instead of ashes, the oil of gladness instead of mourning” (61:3).
“I will greatly rejoice in the LORD; my soul shall exult in my God, for he has clothed me with the garments of salvation” (61:10).
“You shall be called by a new name that the mouth of the LORD will give” (62:2).
“As the bridegroom rejoices over the bride, so shall your God rejoice over you” (62:5).
“In all their affliction he was afflicted, and the angel of his presence saved them; in his love and in his pity he redeemed them” (63:9).
interpretation:
The speaker of chapter 61 is the Servant, now described as anointed with the Spirit. He is a prophet, a king, and a priest. His mission is a series of reversals: good news to the poor, binding up the brokenhearted, liberty for captives, comfort for those who mourn. The promise is of a jubilee, a year of release. The imagery is of the Year of Jubilee in Leviticus 25, when debts were forgiven and slaves went free. The beautiful exchanges are: a crown instead of ashes, gladness instead of mourning, a garment of praise instead of a faint spirit.

When Jesus read this passage in Nazareth, he stopped in the middle of verse 2, after “the year of the LORD’s favor.” He omitted the phrase “and the day of vengeance of our God.” Then he said, “Today this Scripture has been fulfilled in your hearing.” The first coming brings the favor, and the second will bring the vengeance. The two parts are separated by the time of the church.

Chapter 62 expresses God’s passion for his people. He will not keep silent until her righteousness shines like the dawn. She will be called by a new name, “My Delight Is in Her.” “As the bridegroom rejoices over the bride, so shall your God rejoice over you.” This is the language of marriage, as in Hosea. The divine bridegroom delights in his people. Watchmen are posted on the walls who will give God no rest until he makes Jerusalem a praise in the earth.

Chapter 63 begins with a terrifying warrior coming from Edom. His garments are stained red, for he has trodden the winepress alone. It is a picture of God’s judgment on his enemies. Then the prophet looks back with gratitude and prays, remembering the exodus. “In all their affliction he was afflicted.” God suffers with his people. But they rebelled and grieved his Holy Spirit. Even so, the Spirit led them, “like livestock that go down into the valley,” to give them rest.
connection: Jesus announced in Luke 4:18-21 that Isaiah 61 was fulfilled in him. He answered John the Baptist with these signs (Luke 7:22). Matthew 5:4 says, “Blessed are those who mourn, for they shall be comforted.” Ephesians 5:25-27 shows Christ as the bridegroom who presents the church to himself in splendor. Revelation 19:13-15 draws on the warrior with the stained garment, and verse 7 speaks of the marriage of the Lamb. Ephesians 4:30 echoes “do not grieve the Holy Spirit.”
application:
Read Isaiah 61:1-3 as a description of your calling in Christ, and see where you can bring good news to someone who is poor, broken, or bound.

Receive the exchange: ask Jesus to give you a crown instead of ashes and the oil of gladness instead of mourning.

Rest in the truth that God rejoices over you, as a bridegroom over a bride.
prayerPrompts: Thank Jesus for bringing good news to the poor and binding up the brokenhearted.
Tell him what you want him to bind up in you.
Thank him for the year of favor.
